newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 6.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian cricket team has suffered at the hands of English bowler Darren Gough, who took three of the first four wickets in the first Ashes Test at Edgbaston. The Australian innings, which had slumped to 4/28, saw captain Mark Taylor again fail wit the bat - he scored just seven runs. Page 24.

Australian Football League chief executive officer Wayne Jackson announced yesterday the AFL will appeal against a Supreme Court ruling which overturned a nine-match suspension on Carlton's Greg Williams. In response, the Carlton club has said it would b prepared to go the High Court if the AFL appeal is successful. Page 24.

The Brisbane and London Super League teams meet tonight in the first match of the Super League World Cup Challenge, and already the atmosphere is tense, with Broncos chief executive Shane Edwards accusing former Broncos player and now London coach Tony Curie of becoming a "whinging Pom" after his complaints over game schedules. Page 24.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

New South Wales chairman of selectors Barry Want said yesterday ACT Brumbies captain Brett Robinson should be Australia's rugby union Test captain. Want said that of all the captains he had seen play this season, the 27-year-old flanker had been the mostinspirational. Page 42.

Australian golfer Greg Norman was lucky to avoid an ugly incident at the Kemper Open in Washington on Wednesday, when an apparently tipsy spectator wanted to give Norman a mouthful. However, at the time, two police officers were walking with Norman and another two joined him later. Page 42.

The Australian women's hockey team has defeated Britain 3-0 to move further ahead at the Champions Trophy tournament in Berlin. Australia's three goals were scored by Karen Smith, Jenny Morris and Michelle Andrews. Page 39.
THE AGE

Essendon Australian Football League star James Hird is suffering from a stress fracture in his right foot, and is not expected to play for the rest of the season. Hird's injury forced him to leave the field in the game against the Western Bulldogs last Sunday, and he said he may only return in the 1997 season if Essendon reached the finals. Page D5.

The Australian netball team heads into the second match of a three-match series against the South African Proteas with one win under its belt after a 65-48 win in Brisbane on Tuesday. Coach Jill McIntosh said she was pleased with the first match, but wans the team to concentrate on unforced errors in the second. Page D11.

The Hawthorn Australian Football Club is considering a people's referendum on its plans to cover Waverly Park's exposed seating areas. President Ian Dicker said the club will ask for AFL approval if 80 per cent of the potential 700,000 respondents agree ith the plan. Page D10.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian tennis player Pat Rafter will spend today sleeping, eating, and taking in light practice before his semi-final showdown in the French Open tonight. Rafter will meet Spain's Sergi Bruguera, a player known to be a claycourt specialist. Page 112

Australian Socceroos soccer team assistant coach Raul Blanco said sharpshooter Mark Viduka is in doubt for next week's World Cup qualifiers against the Solomon Islands and Tahiti because of a hamstring injury. He is the only player in doubt for the serie. Page 110.

Horse trainer Bob Taylor is wondering why his horse Summer Beau, which won the Hollindale Cup against Shame and All Our Mob and is at 5-1 for the Queensland Derby at Eagle Farm, has been overlooked in the lead up to the race. So far, all the talk has bee about Yippyio (6-4) and Marble Halls (2-1). Page 98.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

New South Wales Deputy Opposition Leader Ron Phillips says the Carr Government's legislation for the privatisation of the New South Wales TAB is flawed and could dramatically cut the TAB's market value. Page 134.

Canberra Raiders five-eighth Laurie Daley will not play in the World Cup Challenge match against Halifax at Bruce Stadium this Sunday due to a calf injury. He will be replaced by Jason Burnham, a player captain Ricky Stuart says would handle the job. Pag 132.

Following news the International Athletic Federation has ratified her world indoor and outdoor records, Australian pole vaulter Emma George has left for Slovakia where she will tackle the European Grand Prix circuit. Page 128.
